# How to illustrate lessons on the Blackboard

Research, 2026-09-03. Question: what should the agent use to draw small explanatory figures (T-accounts, money flows, timelines, tables, K-maps, vectors, waveforms, small graphs) on the dark board, instead of Manim stills?

Four parallel sweeps: declarative diagram languages, hand-drawn/chalk renderers, how the best explainers make figures, and how well LLMs author each format. Prototype and screenshots in `figure-compare/` (open `compare.html` over http; it loads Google Fonts).

## Verdict

**Author figures as inline SVG, generated by a small Node library built on Rough.js, in the page's own fonts and palette. Render, look, fix. Stop rasterising through Manim.**

Why this and not a diagram DSL:

- The figures we draw are *placed*, not *laid out*. A T-account, a timeline, a vector pair, a waveform are exact coordinates. Auto-layout tools (D2, Mermaid, Graphviz) cannot express them; D2's best attempt turned the T-account into a single-column table in the wrong palette (row E in the comparison).
- SVG is the format where an LLM is now strong on the first try and where the fix loop is a numeric edit. SVGBench (2026): Claude Opus 4.6 at 75.6%, up from GPT-4o's 31.8% two years earlier. Every render-and-look study (IntroSVG, Render-in-the-Loop, ReLook) gains 6–8 points from one inspection pass.
- Inline SVG keeps text as text: page font, page colour, selectable, so Explain works on figure labels too. Manim gives a PNG with its own font at a fixed resolution; Typst converts text to paths; D2 embeds 25 KB of WOFF per figure.
- Rough.js adds the chalk stroke for free (multi-stroke, bowing, seeded so re-renders are stable) and has no text API, which is exactly right: numbers stay crisp and aligned because we emit `<text>` ourselves.
- Everything the top explainers do is compatible with this: Distill, Red Blob Games, Khan's Mafs, Byrne's Euclid and Setosa all ship hand-authored or code-generated SVG in the text column. 3Blue1Brown is the outlier (Manim for video) and Manim benchmarks are poor for agents (25–67% zero-shot executability, Claude 2.1% on TheoremExplainAgent).

## Comparison (same figure, five renderers)

| | Renderer | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| A | Manim still (current) | Own font, raster, huge margins, 1.5 s render, API hallucination risk. Drop. |
| B | Rough.js SVG, Crimson Pro | Chalk strokes, page serif, perfect column alignment. Consistent with the lesson text. |
| C | Rough.js SVG, Patrick Hand | Same geometry, handwriting font. Reads as chalk on a board. **Default.** |
| D | Pikchr SVG | Precise, 4 KB, inherits page font, but flat strokes and its own tiny type scale. Good fallback when a figure needs its PIC-style relative placement. |
| E | D2 `--sketch` | Real hand-drawn look but no two-column tables, off-palette fills, WOFF embedded. Use only for graphs with more than ~6 nodes. |

## Design rules to bake in (from Mayer, Tufte, Distill, Red Blob, 3b1b)

1. One idea per figure, at most 7 elements. Split rather than crowd.
2. Labels in place, never a legend. Words go beside the thing they name.
3. One highlight colour (`#9b3a4a`) and only on the causal path: what changed, not everything interesting.
4. Layout mirrors structure: before → after left to right, stacks for quantities, equal heights for balanced sides.
5. Static frames. Motion only when the manner of motion is the lesson.
6. Figure width = text column. No frames, no boxes around the figure, no decoration.
7. Pair every abstract figure with the concrete numbers from the lesson.
8. Balance sheets: side-by-side T-accounts with new lines in the highlight colour (textbook), or the Bank of England stacked-bars form (equal-height assets | liabilities columns, new segments outlined) when the point is proportion.

## Implementation plan for the skill

1. `bin/fig.mjs`: Node + Rough.js, no browser. Templates: `taccount`, `bars` (BoE stacked balance sheet), `flow` (entities + labelled arrows), `timeline`, `table`, `kmap`, `vectors`, `wave` (computed polyline), plus raw primitives for anything else. Emits SVG with `viewBox` only, `currentColor` strokes, text in `var(--fig-font)`.
2. Lesson syntax: `::: fig <template>` with a small YAML/JSON body, rendered by the bridge into an inline `<svg>`; `::: figure path.svg` also inlines instead of `<img>`.
3. Board CSS: load Patrick Hand; `--fig-font: 'Patrick Hand', 'Crimson Pro', serif`; figures span the column; captions stay in the dim serif.
4. Check loop before the figure lands: a deterministic lint (label bbox overlaps by character-count width, out-of-viewBox, arrow endpoints on box edges), then a PNG render (`qlmanage` or resvg) the agent looks at. Deterministic first: vision-only judges miss layout errors (vTikZ, EduIllustrate).
5. Escalation: D2 for graphs beyond ~6 nodes (strip its `@font-face`), Vega-Lite or matplotlib with `svg.fonttype='none'` for real axes and ticks.
